newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products flat to weaker in dull market.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products flat to weaker in dull market.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were flat to weaker in a dull market on Thursday, traders said.
The attraction of shipping gas oil to Asia was diminishing as tonnage becomes increasingly hard to find and disquiet about the firmness of Singapore prices rises.
"The arb is still there at $2-3 a tonne, but it's a long way to go to make that," said one trader.
The large 50kt Constanza cargo for 5-10 May was still available and a Tuapse cargo was sold at fob high quotes +$4. Italian spec was pegged at high fob quotes +3-4.
Diesel was holding firm at high fob EN590 quotes +$2-3.
Fuel oil markets were very quiet although an 80,000 tonne cargo of high sulphur end-May barrels from Italy was believed sold to a Dutch trader with regular needs in Romania and Cuba.
The high sulphur market again looked weak, with May well supplied with material. Swaps recovered slightly from Wednesday's $74 to around $74.50/$75.50 with physical prices stuck at $75/$76.
Traders said the grade was still fundamentally weak, with some anticipating it had further to come still after this week's $4 fall.
Gasoline was flat in a dull market.
Some players were expecting prices to firm into as May approached.
Naphtha eased on negative sentiment related to Sonatrach's decision not to give permission for the loading of larger naphtha cargoes out of Skikda.
Traders said the move would hit lifters hoping to move large cargoes Eastward and could weigh on European prices if they decided to keep the material in the region.
Traders said exporters had been planning to move at least two large May naphtha cargoes East before the suspension of double stem loadings. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
